title: Supports multi-dimenstional grouping
body:
<!-- Please provide the issue number here if any -->

## Changelog Entry

### Breaking changes

- `useGroupActivities` hook is being deprecated in favor of the `useGroupActivitiesByName` hook. The hook will be removed on or after 2027-05-04

### Added

- Added multi-dimensional grouping, `styleOptions.groupActivitiesBy`, and `useGroupActivitiesByName` hook, in PR [#5471](https://github.com/microsoft/BotFramework-WebChat/pull/5471), by [@compulim](https://github.com/compulim)
   - Existing behavior will be kept and activities will be grouped by `sender` followed by `status`
   - `useGroupActivitiesByName` is favored over the existing `useGroupActivities` hook for performance reason
   - Middleware which support the new grouping name init argument should only compute the grouping if they match the grouping name, or the grouping name is not specified, otherwise, should do nothing and call the downstream middleware

## Description

Today, despite Web Chat support custom grouping, it is limited to two dimensions (sender followed by status.)

Tomorrow, we will support multi-dimensional grouping with custom grouping and grouping order.

In the future, we should consider moving the timestamp and send status from activity into activity grouping component.

## Design

### New `styleOptions.groupActivitiesBy`

`styleOptions.groupActivitiesBy` is an array containing name of groupings in its respective order, default to `['sender', 'status']`.

### `groupActivitiesMiddleware` enhancement

`groupActivitiesMiddleware` will support initialization argument to indicate what grouping name is supported by the said middleware. The new signature is:

```ts
(name: string | undefined) =>
  next =>
    ({ activities: WebChatActivity[] }) =>
      {
        [key: string]: WebChatActivity[][]
      }
```

Notes: as this is middleware, the computation should always look at result from upstream and propagate it as needed to downstream.

If `name` is `undefined`, the middleware should always compute the grouping. Otherwise, it should match the `name`.

If `name` is not interesting to the targeting middleware, the middleware can simply return `undefined` to indicate that it is not participating in the said grouping name.

```ts
(name: string) => undefined
```

### `<DecoratorComposer>` to support "activity grouping" type

`<DecoratorComposer>` will support new decorator type `"activity grouping"`. The middleware signature is:

```ts
type ActivityGroupingDecoratorMiddleware =
  (type: 'activity grouping') => 
    next => 
      React.ComponentType<{ 
        activities: WebChatActivity[],
        children?: ReactNode | undefined,
        groupingName: string
      }>
```

### New `useGroupActivitiesByName` hook

`useGroupActivitiesByName` is a new hook for running grouping middleware by name, instead of running all grouping middleware at once. The signature is:

```ts
useGroupActivitiesByName():
  (activities: WebChatActivity[], groupingName: string) => WebChatActivity[][]
```

Unlike `useGroupActivities` which does not validate its result, the new `useGroupActivitiesByName` will perform validation and make sure all activities are grouped and no extraneous activities will appear in the grouping. If violation is detected, it will automatically fallback to activities group by themselves.

Current `useGroupActivities` will be deprecated in favor of the new `useGroupActivitiesByName` hook.

### Internal: new `RenderingActivities` and `GroupedRenderingActivities` context

`RenderingActivities` will compute what activities need to be rendered using `activityMiddleware`. The result can be retrieved by the `useGetRenderActivityCallback` hook.

`GroupedRenderingActivities` extends the `RenderingActivities` by returning a tree structure with grouping information, including activities, child tree, key (of first activity) and grouping name.

### Internal: new `ChatHistoryDOM` context

The existing `activityElementRef` used in `<BasicTranscript>` is replaced by a new context. To get what rendered DOM element of an activity, use the `useActivityElementMapRef` hook. The key of the map is activity key and the value is DOM element.

```ts
useActivityElementMapRef(): RefObject<Map<string, HTMLElement>>
```

(Please refers to the [design](#design) section.)
